# Daily report format

This document is the **single format baseline** for every report under `reports/daily/`. The `job-discovery` skill must read it before creating or updating any daily report. If this document conflicts with the skill body or another note, this document wins on structure; the skill still wins on matching logic.

## File location and updates

- One file per local calendar day: `reports/daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md`
- Create the directory if it does not exist
- When today's file already exists, **keep existing content** and only append new findings or new evidence; never overwrite, delete or silently downgrade an entry that was already confirmed
- Deduplication key: the job's canonical URL (within a platform and across platforms); when no canonical URL exists, fall back to `source + company + title + location` and flag a possible duplicate

Cross-day memory, application records and the run audit live in `reports/job-index.json` and `reports/runs/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl`; their rules are in `job-index-and-audit.md`. They are not part of the daily report and are never pushed to `reportRepo`.

## Language and presentation

- Write all human-readable text in `preferredReportLanguage` from `job-hunter.config.json`. Default to **English** when the field is absent, empty or unsupported, and say so in the final summary.
- Translate the human-readable layer only: title, section headings, table headers, labels (e.g. `Not specified`, `All Germany`, `Exception note`), relative times (e.g. `2 days ago`) and annotation markers (e.g. `[reported MM-DD]`, `[applied MM-DD]`, `⚠️ possible duplicate`, `⚠️ possibly applied MM-DD`).
- Do not translate company names, job titles, technical terms, posted keywords, URLs, dates in `YYYY-MM-DD` or `MM-DD`, index/audit field names, or the priority prompt (`You'd be a top applicant`) and marker `Top applicant`.
- The structure is fixed regardless of language: the same section order, table columns, column order and counts.
- Use **tables** as the main presentation so the report is scannable
- Do not restate long JD passages; do not paste full JDs
- Do not add match scores, rankings, recommendation levels or star ratings, and do not evaluate the candidate profile. The only ordering exception is the platform's own prompt (section 2); never compute one

## Section order

The body starts at the title line and goes straight into tables; no metadata table and no search-scope table:

```markdown
# Daily Job Findings — YYYY-MM-DD
```

The title is part of the human-readable layer: translate `Daily Job Findings` into `preferredReportLanguage` and keep the ` — YYYY-MM-DD` suffix unchanged. The section names below are written in English for reference and are translated the same way.

1. Run summary
2. Matched jobs
3. Feed-sourced jobs — **only when matching feed hiring posts exist**
4. Needs manual review — **only when there are entries**
5. Excluded jobs — **always the last job table**, after matched, feed and review
6. Exception note — **only when the run failed or was largely unusable**, at the very end

A normal run has only sections 1, 2 and 5; sections 3, 4 and 6 appear conditionally and must never be written as an empty "None". Excluded jobs always come last among the job tables so the actionable rows stay on top.

After that, append "Evidence and consistency rules" and "Cross-day repeats and updates", in that fixed order.

### 1. Run summary

```markdown
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Search sources | LinkedIn (list the platforms actually searched per `sources`) |
| Result pages opened | N |
| Cards skipped before opening | N |
| Expired / closed (skipped) | N |
| Already applied (skipped) | N |
| Job detail pages opened | N |
| JDs read successfully | N |
| Matched | N |
| Feed-sourced jobs | N |
| Needs manual review | N |
| Confirmed non-match (excluded) | N |
| Of which cross-day repeats | N |
```

- Only fill numbers the browser session can support; write `cannot determine` when unknown, and **never estimate**
- Search-result card count ≠ opened job pages; never mix them
- "Cards skipped before opening" counts only cards whose title clearly names a different role family, or that are clearly outside the configured country/location, and that were therefore not opened. They never appear in the excluded table
- "Expired / closed" counts only links that turned out to be 404, redirected away from the job, or explicitly stopped accepting applications. They never appear in the excluded table
- Self-check: matched + review + excluded = pages with a successfully read JD
- `Feed-sourced jobs` are post-only matches from the LinkedIn feed; they are not part of the JD inspection sum
- "Already applied" and "Expired / closed" both stay out of that sum: the first is decided by the index, the second by the page

### 2. Matched jobs

Group by **city** (`### Munich (13/30)`, `### Berlin (13/30)`, `### Hamburg (4/30)` …), and order each city by **company size**, never by a computed match quality. Matched vacancies that carry the platform's priority prompt go into one leading group first (see below).

- When `locations` is configured, use the configured city names as headings.
- When `locations` is missing or empty (nationwide run), the city comes from each job page; group by the cities actually found. When a page shows only a country (e.g. `Germany`) or is nationwide remote, use `### All Germany` or `### All Germany (Remote)`. Never invent a city to fit an old heading.

The number in parentheses after a city heading is that city's **share of matches**: `matches in this city / total matches today`. The denominator counts only rows in today's matched table, excluding excluded and review rows. Cities without matches do not appear here.

#### Priority group: `You'd be a top applicant`

Matched jobs with the verified prompt (currently LinkedIn Premium, `linkedinPremium: true`) form one group at the top of section 2, before all city groups:

```markdown
### You'd be a top applicant (3/30)
```

- Use the fixed heading `You'd be a top applicant` in every language; the number is `rows with the prompt / total matches today`.
- Same columns; sort by `sortBy` / `sortDirection` inside the group.
- City is not a column: start each Notes cell with the city, e.g. `Berlin; English JD; Full-time`. The row still counts in its city's share heading.
- Omit the group when empty. The prompt never creates a match; a failed job goes to the excluded table instead.

Ordering rules:

- Follow `sortBy` (currently only `companySize`) and `sortDirection` (`asc` / `desc`, default `asc`)
- Company size uses the range shown on the page and compares the **lower bound**: `11-50` → 11, `10001+` → 10001, `9,000` → 9000
- Rows with the same size keep discovery order
- When `sortBy` is missing or unknown, keep discovery order
- After sorting, renumber the `#` column sequentially in the final display order across the priority group and all city groups, and update any internal references (e.g. "same JD as #22")

Fixed columns:

```markdown
| # | Source | Company | Size | Title | Mode | Posted | Matched keywords | Easy Apply | Cover letter | Notes | Link |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
```

Column rules:

| Column | Rule |
|---|---|
| # | Sequential in final display order, across the priority group and after city grouping and sorting |
| Source | Platform name from `sources`, e.g. `LinkedIn`, `Indeed`; add the domain when the name alone is ambiguous |
| Company | The company field on the job page; when the poster ≠ the actual employer, put the poster here and the employer in Notes |
| Size | The company size shown on the page, e.g. `51-200`, `9,000`, `10001+`; write `Not specified` when absent |
| Title | Keep as published, including (m/f/d), (all genders) and similar suffixes; never put a pipe `|` inside a title, use `·` instead |
| Mode | `On-site` / `Hybrid` / `Remote` as shown; when the page has no such field write `Not specified` and move the row to the review table; add ⚠️ and explain in Notes when it conflicts with the JD body |
| Posted | Relative time (`2 days ago`, `19 hours ago`); mark reposts as `(reposted)` |
| Matched keywords | Only **configured** terms that actually appear in the JD, comma-separated; never add unconfigured technologies |
| Easy Apply | `Yes` when the page shows a one-click apply button on the platform (e.g. LinkedIn "Easy Apply", Indeed "Indeed Apply"), `No` when the apply path clearly leaves the platform or requires an external form, `Unknown` when it cannot be determined |
| Cover letter | `Yes` when the page or application form explicitly says a cover letter is required, `No` when it explicitly says cover letter is optional or not needed, `Unknown` when neither is stated. When the job remains in the report, the value is `Yes`, and `isNeededCover` is `true` in config, the agent copies `cover-letter-template.md` as-is and fills only its placeholders; the result is saved under `reports/cover-letters/<company-slug>/<jobId>.md`. The decision uses only config + this field |
| Notes | Only facts verifiable on the page: main stack, level, contract arrangement, poster/employer mismatch, field conflicts; ≤ about 60 characters; no "great fit" or "recommended" language. Markers follow "Cross-day repeats and updates". Start Notes with the city in the priority group; elsewhere a prompted row adds `Top applicant` |
| Link | `[Open](URL)`, pointing to the canonical job URL actually visited in this run |

City is not a table column: it comes from the section heading (`### Munich (13/30)`), or from the start of Notes inside the priority group. Location details that disagree with the heading (e.g. a role in Pullach, or a remote scope limited to EMEA) go into Notes.

Employment type is a filter, not a column; when it matters for judgment (contract work, parental-leave cover, part-time) write it in Notes.

JD language is also a filter, not a column: matched jobs already satisfy `jdLanguages.include`. When the language cannot be determined and the job goes to the review table, Notes must say "language unknown" and why.

When a job matched because of "German JD + JD explicitly names English as the working language", Notes must state that evidence (e.g. "German JD, names English as team language"); never infer it from the company's international profile.

### 3. Feed-sourced jobs

**Only when at least one matching feed hiring post exists.** Do not write an empty section. This section is filled by the `linkedin-feed-jobs` skill and must be preserved by `job-discovery`.

- Only confirmed matches: the role and location match the config. Non-matching hiring posts are not listed here, not in the review table and not in the excluded table.
- The author does not need to be in the user's following list; a matching job from a stranger, a 2nd/3rd-degree contact or a company page still counts.
- Only role and location are mandatory. A post that names only those two is included; a conflicting stack, work mode, employment type, seniority or language goes into Notes, never into a drop.
- Do not infer a company, role or location the post does not state.
- Fixed columns:

```markdown
| # | Source | Company | Title | Location | Mode | Posted | Matched keywords | Notes | Link |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | LinkedIn Feed | Example GmbH | Senior Frontend Engineer | Berlin | Hybrid | 2h ago | React, TypeScript | 来自 feed; hiring manager post | [Open](URL) |
```

- `Source` is always `LinkedIn Feed`.
- `Matched keywords` lists only configured terms actually named; write `None matched` when the post names a stack but no configured term matches, and `Not stated` when no stack is named.
- `Notes` must start with `来自 feed` (use `From feed` when the report language is not Chinese), followed by one short verifiable fact.
- `Link` is the post permalink; write `Link unavailable` when no permalink exists.
- Deduplicate against matched, review and existing feed rows. A job appears in only one section.
- Renumber the `#` column after merging.

### 4. Needs manual review

**Only when there are entries**. When empty, omit the whole section; never write "None".

Use the same table structure as section 2, and state in **Notes**:

- which check is unknown (title / language / keywords / work mode / employment type)
- the concrete reason it is missing or ambiguous (JD did not load, too short, truncated, mixed language, page does not expose the field, …)

Prompted rows come first in discovery order and start Notes with `Top applicant`; the prompt never makes an unknown check a match.

Unknown items **must not** be written as matched or excluded.

### 5. Excluded jobs

**Always the last job table**, written after matched, feed and review. A separate section, not counted in the main table. Fixed columns:

```markdown
| # | Source | Company | Title | City | Mode | Posted | Easy Apply | Cover letter | Exclusion reason | Link |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
```

- Posted: relative time (`2 days ago`, `19 hours ago`), mark reposts as `(reposted)`; write `Not specified` when the page does not show it
- City: the location shown on the job page; write `Not specified` when absent, never infer
- Exclusion reason must name the **dimension** (JD language / job title / technical keywords / work mode / employment type / seniority (when enabled) / poster type (staffing agency)) plus one short piece of evidence (e.g. the German original fragment, the missing keyword, the mode or type shown on the page, the industry, or an "our client" phrase in the JD)
- Group similar reasons together (e.g. all German JDs) so the table is scannable
- Do not paste long JD passages
- Duplicate relationships (same role in different cities, bilingual copies) may be noted, but must never be double-counted as matches
- A prompted job that failed a check is listed here with only the failed dimension; the prompt is never an exclusion reason
- Jobs skipped at the card stage (clearly wrong title or out of scope) and never opened **do not appear here**; they count only in "Cards skipped before opening"
- **The link column is mandatory**, format `[Open](URL)`, pointing to the job page actually opened in this run, so every row can be checked
- Excluded-table URLs are for manual checking only and **must never be used as a cross-day dedup key** (see "Cross-day repeats and updates")

### 6. Exception note

**Only when one of these happens, and always at the very end**; a normal run never includes it, and routine search parameters (city radius, paging method, time zone) are never listed:

- the run failed or stopped: expired login, CAPTCHA, rate limit, no browser tool
- the run did not finish: result pages left unread, stopped early
- widespread failure: a large share of jobs could not be judged because JDs were unreadable, truncated or missing key fields

Length limit: 3 lines, covering only three things — what happened, how many rows it affected, where it stopped. No disclaimer-style essay.

## Evidence and consistency rules

- Use only facts visible on the job page or verified in the browser session
- Every active matching dimension must be independent and traceable to concrete evidence
- Mark a job as matched only when every active dimension is confirmed
- Write `Not specified` for missing fields; never infer location, work mode, employment type or posting date
- Keep URLs exactly as found; never assemble or invent one
- A job appears at most once in the same report; a match and an exclusion never both count
- `Feed-sourced jobs` use only the post text. Never open an external link to verify them.
- Feed jobs are matched on role + location only; technical keywords, work mode, employment type, seniority and JD language never exclude a row.
- A non-matching feed hiring post is ignored and must never be listed in any section, including the excluded table.
- A feed job appears only in the feed section; if the same job is already in matched or review, do not duplicate it.
- The priority prompt is personal Premium UI text: ordering metadata only, never a matching dimension or an inferred signal
- Every daily report uses the same section order and table columns so reports stay comparable
- Do not output candidate-fit, salary-expectation or visa judgments

## Cross-day repeats and updates

A daily report is a **snapshot of that day**, not a cumulative list. Cross-day repeats are still listed; they are only annotated, never removed.

Comparison baseline: prefer `reports/job-index.json`, which covers all history; when the index is missing, fall back to the previous 7 local dates under `reports/daily/`. Only jobs that ever entered the **matched table** or the **review table** count as already reported; excluded and expired entries do not.

| Situation | Handling |
|---|---|
| `firstReportedOn` is set in the index | List the job in today's report as usual and append `[reported MM-DD]` (from `firstReportedOn`) to Notes; never delete it, reclassify it or move it to the excluded table |
| `appliedOn` is set in the index | Do not open or judge it; count it under "Already applied (skipped)" only; it must not appear in any job table |
| Previously appeared only in the excluded table | Not part of dedup; re-evaluate it today |
| No index and no earlier reports | Skip this step and add no marker |

- Markers affect readability only and never reduce the number of jobs actually opened today
- The same URL still appears at most once in today's report
- "Of which cross-day repeats" = rows in today's matched table carrying `[reported …]`
- Always use `MM-DD` in historical markers to avoid cross-year ambiguity

### Same role, different ID

The same job may exist on one platform under several job IDs, in multi-city versions or in bilingual versions; the same job may also appear on several platforms. Compare `normalized company + normalized title + city`; when it is a match and the job ID differs, write `⚠️ possible duplicate` in Notes, or `⚠️ possibly applied MM-DD` when the other posting was applied to. Annotate only — never merge, delete or change counts. Normalization rules are in `job-index-and-audit.md`.

### Application marker

After the user confirms an application, append `[applied MM-DD]` to that job's Notes and write `appliedOn` in the index. The marker does not change today's matched/review decision or any count.

### Cover letter generation

Read `isNeededCover` from `job-hunter.config.json` (default `false`). Generate a cover letter for a job that remains in the report (`matched` or `review`) only when `isNeededCover` is `true` and `coverLetter` is `Yes`. The decision uses only those two inputs; do not add extra criteria. Copy `cover-letter-template.md` exactly as the user wrote it: keep its structure, sections, wording and order, and replace only the placeholders that exist in it. Do not rewrite, restructure, add or remove sections, or add content the template does not ask for. Save it locally under:

`reports/cover-letters/<company-slug>/<jobId>.md`

- Fill only the template's own placeholders using facts from the job page. Map each placeholder by the wording around it (job title, team, product, city, JD requirement) and never change the surrounding text. Do not add extra paragraphs, sections or requirements. If a placeholder cannot be filled from the page, leave it unchanged and tell the user; do not guess.
- Never fabricate experience, achievements, or motivations.
- Do not submit automatically — the draft is for manual review and sending.
- Skip jobs where `coverLetter` is `No` or `Unknown`. When `isNeededCover` is `false`, do not draft a cover letter.
- If `cover-letter-template.md` is missing, do not invent or reuse another template. Stop that step and tell the user to copy `cover-letter-template-example.md` to `cover-letter-template.md` first.

## Updating an existing report

- Keep existing entries and their evidence
- Preserve the `Feed-sourced jobs` section and its rows when updating the report
- Add or correct only when there is new evidence
- Never silently rewrite an old conclusion because the configuration changed; when new configuration flips a decision, state the reason in the new entry or in Notes

# Glassdoor

Reference for `sources: ["Glassdoor"]`, using the German site `https://www.glassdoor.de` when the configured country is Germany. Use the matching country domain otherwise (for example `glassdoor.com`, `glassdoor.co.uk`).

Glassdoor changes its job-search markup frequently and sometimes gates results. Confirm each control in the live page; when a control is missing, use the stated fallback.

## 1. Search entry

Open `https://www.glassdoor.de/Job/jobs.htm` and submit `jobSearchPrompt` **verbatim** in the keyword field (`sc.keyword`). Use the location control for `countries`/`locations`.

- Do not translate or shorten the prompt.
- If the modern search page uses a different path, follow the visible "Jobs" navigation rather than guessing a URL.
- Signed-out visitors may be shown a subset of results or a sign-in prompt; treat that as an access boundary (section 5), not as an empty result.

## 2. Filter mapping

| Config | Glassdoor control | Mapping |
|---|---|---|
| `lookbackHours` | Date posted | ≤24 → `Last 24 hours`; ≤72 → `Last 3 days`; ≤168 → `Last 7 days`; ≤336 → `Last 14 days`; otherwise `Last 30 days` or no filter. Never narrower than `lookbackHours`. |
| `employmentTypes` | Job type | `Full-time`, `Part-time`, `Contract`, `Temporary`, `Internship`. No reliable `Volunteer` equivalent — judge on the page. |
| `workModes` | Remote | Glassdoor exposes a `Remote` filter in some markets. `Hybrid` / `On-site` usually have none: select nothing and judge on the page. |
| `seniority.include` | — | No equivalent. Judge from the title or explicit level wording. |
| `countries`, `locations` | Location | Country comes from the domain; configured cities go into the location field. With no `locations`, keep country level. |

Do not add filters that are not in the config (company rating, salary, industry, company size). Glassdoor's rating and salary widgets are not matching dimensions.

Verify the filters are visibly applied. If Glassdoor resets them, re-apply or fall back to reading each posting.

## 3. Result extraction

- Job listing ID: the `jobListingId` query parameter, or the `JV_...` / `KO...KE...` segment in the listing URL.
- Canonical URL: the listing URL that contains `jobListingId`, with tracking parameters removed (keep the listing ID and job title slug).
- Company, title, location and posting age come from the card; the detail page wins on conflicts.
- Glassdoor often redirects to the employer's own career site. Keep the Glassdoor listing URL as the canonical link, and record the employer URL in the note only when it is visible on the page.

## 4. Pagination

Advance with the results pagination control (`p=2`, `p=3`, …) or infinite scroll, whichever the page uses. Stop when:

- postings are older than `lookbackHours`;
- no further results load;
- the same listing IDs repeat;
- a sign-in prompt, CAPTCHA or rate limit appears.

## 5. Access boundaries

Glassdoor gates some listings and some pages behind sign-in. When that happens:

1. Stop this source; do not attempt to work around the gate.
2. Record it in `limitations` as `glassdoor: sign-in required`.
3. Continue with the remaining sources.

Never solve a CAPTCHA, never create an account, and never submit an application or "easy apply".

## 6. Application-process fields

Record these while the job page is open. They are informational only and never affect match/review/excluded classification.

**Easy Apply:** `Yes` when the detail page shows an "Easy Apply" button that applies within Glassdoor; `No` when the apply button clearly redirects to the employer's site or an external application form; `Unknown` when neither is visible. Never infer it from badges or search ranking. Never submit an application or use the "easy apply" flow.

**Cover letter:** `Yes` when the page or the application form explicitly states a cover letter is required; `No` when it explicitly states cover letter is optional or not needed; `Unknown` when neither is stated. Do not open the apply flow just to check — record only what is visible on the job page.

## 7. Known quirks

- `glassdoor.de` serves German UI and German-language listings; a listing's own language may still be English. Judge the JD language from the posting, never from the site locale.
- Ratings, salary estimates and "best places to work" badges are not filters and must not influence classification.
- Some listings are aggregator copies of other boards; the same role may appear on LinkedIn or Indeed with a different ID — soft dedup will flag it.
- Redirects to employer career sites can lose the original posting date; when the Glassdoor card shows a date, use it.

| Config | Indeed control | Mapping |
|---|---|---|
| `lookbackHours` | Date posted | ≤24 → `Last 24 hours`; ≤72 → `Last 3 days`; ≤168 → `Last 7 days`; ≤336 → `Last 14 days`; otherwise `Last 30 days` or no filter. Never choose a window narrower than `lookbackHours`. |
| `employmentTypes` | Job type | `Full-time`, `Part-time`, `Contract`, `Temporary`, `Internship`. Indeed has no reliable `Volunteer` equivalent — skip that value and judge on the page. |
| `workModes` | Remote | Indeed exposes a `Remote` filter. `Hybrid` and `On-site` usually have no filter: select nothing for them and judge on the page. |
| `seniority.include` | — | No equivalent. Skip the UI filter and judge from the title or explicit level wording. |
| `countries`, `locations` | Where | Country comes from the domain; put configured cities in the location field. With no `locations`, leave it at country level. |

Do not add filters that are not in the config (salary estimate, company rating, `Easy apply`, urgency). Indeed sometimes carries a URL form of the same filters (`fromage`, `jt`, `sc`); they are acceptable shortcuts only after confirming the page shows the same selection.

Verify the applied filters are visible on the results page. If Indeed drops them, apply them again or fall back to reading each posting.

## 3. Result extraction

- Job key: the `jk` parameter on the card link or apply button, e.g. `jk=7f3c9a1b2d4e5f60` (usually 16 hex characters). A card without `jk` is not usable — skip it and count it as a card skip.
- Canonical URL: `https://<country-domain>/viewjob?jk=<jk>`. Strip tracking parameters (`?vjs=`, `?tk=`, `?from=`, `?advn=`, `?xpse=`, `?xkcb=`); keep `jk`.
- Company and location come from the card; the detail page wins on conflicts.
- Indeed shows sponsored cards that repeat organic results — deduplicate by `jk` before opening.

## 4. Pagination

Advance with the results pagination control (or `start=10`, `start=20`, … if the page exposes it). Stop when:

- postings are older than `lookbackHours`;
- the page shows no further results;
- the same `jk` set repeats;
- a login wall, CAPTCHA or rate limit appears.

## 5. Access boundaries

Indeed may interrupt with a login prompt, a "verify you are human" challenge or a rate limit after several pages. Stop this source at that boundary, record it in `limitations`, and continue with other sources. Never solve a CAPTCHA, never create an account, never use the "Easy apply" flow.

## 6. Application-process fields

Record these while the job page is open. They are informational only and never affect match/review/excluded classification.

**Easy Apply:** `Yes` when the detail page shows an "Indeed Apply" or "Easy Apply" button that applies within Indeed; `No` when the apply button clearly redirects to the employer's site or an external application form; `Unknown` when neither is visible. Never infer it from badges or search ranking. Never use the "Easy apply" flow itself.

**Cover letter:** `Yes` when the page or the application form explicitly states a cover letter is required; `No` when it explicitly states cover letter is optional or not needed; `Unknown` when neither is stated. Do not open the apply flow just to check — record only what is visible on the job page.

## 7. Known quirks

- Country is encoded in the domain: use `de.indeed.com` for Germany, and so on. Search results and job IDs are not portable across domains.
- Sponsored and organic cards duplicate each other; deduplicate on `jk`.
- The job page URL form differs from the card link; always normalise to `/viewjob?jk=<jk>`.
- Salary and company-rating badges are not filters and must not influence classification.

# Job index, deduplication and run audit

This document defines Job Hunter's local memory layer. The `job-discovery` skill must follow it on every run; the daily report structure still follows `daily-report-format.md`.

## 1. Files

| File | Purpose | Committed |
|---|---|---|
| `reports/job-index.json` | Cross-day job index and application record | No — Git-ignored, local only |
| `reports/runs/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` | Run audit log, one line per run | No — Git-ignored, local only |

Never push these two files to `reportRepo`. `reportRepo` receives only the day's daily report.

## 2. Job index schema

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "updatedAt": "2026-11-10",
  "jobs": {
    "LinkedIn:4487182341": {
      "jobId": "4487182341",
      "source": "LinkedIn",
      "url": "https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/4487182341/",
      "company": "immobilien.de",
      "title": "Senior Software Engineer",
      "city": "Berlin",
      "firstSeen": "2026-11-08",
      "lastSeen": "2026-11-10",
      "firstReportedOn": "2026-11-08",
      "status": "matched",
      "appliedOn": null,
      "easyApply": "unknown",
      "coverLetter": "unknown",
      "note": ""
    }
  }
}
```

Field rules:

- Keys use `<source>:<jobId>`, e.g. `LinkedIn:4487182341`, `Indeed:7f3c9a1b2d4e5f60`. `source` must match the platform name in `sources`.
- When the platform exposes no job ID, fall back to `source + canonical URL` as the key; one URL yields exactly one entry.
- Bare job IDs in an older index are treated as LinkedIn. Keep their keys as they are; do not rewrite them in bulk.
- `source`: the canonical platform name (`LinkedIn`, `Indeed`, `Glassdoor`), not a configured domain alias; this keeps `glassdoor.de` and `Glassdoor` from creating two entries.
- `status`: `matched` / `review` / `excluded` / `expired`, recording the **most recent** decision.
- `firstSeen`: the date the job was first opened.
- `lastSeen`: the date it was most recently opened or re-confirmed.
- `firstReportedOn`: the date it first entered the **matched or review table**; `null` if it never did. Excluded days do not count.
- `appliedOn`: the date the user confirmed an application; `null` otherwise.
- `easyApply`: whether the posting offers a one-click apply path on the platform (`yes`, `no`, `unknown`). Read from the job page only; never infer from applicant count, search ranking or JD text.
- `coverLetter`: whether the posting requires a cover letter (`yes`, `no`, `unknown`). Read from the job page or application form only; never infer from company size or industry.
- `note`: optional, verifiable facts from the page only, no judgment.
- Update only the relevant fields and preserve unknown fields; never rewrite the whole object or touch other entries.

Create the index when missing. When it cannot be parsed, back it up to `reports/job-index.json.bak`, rebuild an empty index, and say so in the run's chat output.

## 3. Read order

1. Prefer `reports/job-index.json`; it covers all history.
2. When the index is missing, read the previous 7 local dates under `reports/daily/` as a one-time bootstrap and recover only URLs, status and first-seen dates.
3. When neither exists, start from an empty index.

## 4. Deduplication and reuse rules

**Hard dedup**: the same job ID or canonical URL on one platform is the same job; an identical canonical URL across platforms is also treated as the same job.

- `appliedOn` is set in the index → **do not open, do not judge, do not list in any job table**; count it only as "Already applied (skipped)".
- Entry exists with latest status `matched` / `review` → still reopen and judge it today (it may have closed or changed), and append `[reported MM-DD]` to Notes using `firstReportedOn`.
- Entry exists with latest status `excluded` / `expired` → re-evaluate today as usual, add no `[reported]` marker; if it matches today, set `firstReportedOn` to today.

**Soft dedup (likely same role, different ID)**: the same role often has multiple job IDs, multi-city versions or bilingual versions on one platform, and is often listed on several platforms.

- Comparison key: `normalized company + normalized title + city`. When comparing across platforms, **do not** include the platform name in the key.
- Normalization: lowercase; strip punctuation, extra spaces and gender markers such as `(m/w/d)`, `(f/m/d)`, `(all genders)`; strip legal suffixes (GmbH, AG, SE, Inc, Ltd, LLC, GmbH & Co. KG).
- Do not strip level words such as Senior / Junior / Lead, and do not merge different cities.
- On a soft-dedup hit with a different job ID → write `⚠️ possible duplicate` in Notes; when the other posting has `appliedOn`, write `⚠️ possibly applied MM-DD`.
- Annotate only — never delete, reclassify or merge counts.

## 5. Application recording

Trigger: the user says "I applied to X", "mark these as applied", or names the jobs explicitly.

1. Locate the job: prefer today's report, then historical reports, then the index by URL or "company + title".
2. Set `appliedOn` to today and keep `status` unchanged.
3. If the job already appears in today's report, append `[applied MM-DD]` to Notes; otherwise update the index only.
4. When it cannot be identified uniquely, ask one clarifying question. Never guess and never mark a batch.
5. Do not change the daily report's counts or decisions.

## 6. Run audit schema

Path: `reports/runs/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` (split by local date; several runs in one day append several lines, never overwrite).

```json
{
  "runAt": "2026-11-10T09:30:00+01:00",
  "finishedAt": "2026-11-10T10:02:00+01:00",
  "durationSeconds": 1920,
  "scope": { "countries": ["Germany"], "locations": [] },
  "sources": ["LinkedIn"],
  "uiFilters": {
    "LinkedIn": {
      "datePosted": "Past 24 hours",
      "employmentTypes": ["Full-time"],
      "workModes": ["Remote", "Hybrid", "On-site"],
      "seniority": null
    }
  },
  "prompt": "…verbatim jobSearchPrompt…",
  "resultsBySource": { "LinkedIn": 300 },
  "resultCount": 300,
  "resultPagesOpened": 5,
  "resultPagesBySource": { "LinkedIn": 5 },
  "searchedBySource": { "LinkedIn": "completed" },
  "cardsSkipped": 0,
  "postingsInspected": 120,
  "expired": 0,
  "appliedSkipped": 4,
  "matched": 23,
  "review": 12,
  "excluded": 85,
  "crossDayRepeats": 10,
  "possibleDuplicates": 2,
  "stopReason": "results older than lookbackHours",
  "limitations": []
}
```

Rules:

- `runAt` is when the search **started**, not when the report was written; `finishedAt` is when the report, index and audit were finished; `durationSeconds` is their integer difference.
- All three use the local time zone with a UTC offset (e.g. `+08:00`). Write `null` when unknown; never estimate.
- Record only numbers the browser session can support; write `null` when unknown, never estimate.
- `sources` records the platforms actually attempted, in configured order; `searchedBySource` marks each platform `completed` / `failed` / `skipped` (with the reason).
- `uiFilters` is grouped by platform and records only the filters that platform actually offered; a platform without UI filters gets an empty object.
- `resultsBySource` and `resultCount` come from the count the results page displays; write `null` when it shows none. Page counts go into `resultPagesBySource`; `resultPagesOpened` is the total. Older logs used `linkedinResultCount`, which equals today's `resultsBySource.LinkedIn` — read old data compatibly and never rewrite old lines.
- `stopReason` is a short phrase explaining why paging stopped, e.g. `results older than lookbackHours`, `no more pages`, `login required`, `cap reached`.
- `limitations` lists only limitations that actually occurred (CAPTCHA, rate limit, filter that could not be applied, …); empty on a normal run.
- Several runs on one day append several lines; never merge them.
- `postingsInspected` / `matched` / `review` / `excluded` are **this run's** counts; the daily report's run-summary table is the **day total**. The summary email needs both; never conflate them.

## 7. Retention and cleanup

- Never delete index entries or audit logs automatically.
- Only export, clean or rebuild when the user asks, and confirm the scope first.

# LinkedIn

Reference implementation for `sources: ["LinkedIn"]`. Follow this file for the search, filters and result extraction; the filtering and reporting rules stay in `SKILL.md`.

## 1. Search entry

Open LinkedIn Jobs and use its AI job search, entering `jobSearchPrompt` **verbatim**.

- Do not rewrite, split, translate or append cities.
- Submit once. Re-submitting a changed prompt invalidates the filters you already set.
- If the AI search is not available in the account's UI, fall back to the plain keyword search with the same prompt text and say so in `limitations`.

## 2. Filter mapping

Text inside `jobSearchPrompt` is not a filter: LinkedIn does not reliably enforce "24 hours", "full-time" or similar wording written in the prompt. Set the filters in LinkedIn's filter bar after submitting, and verify they show as active before reading results.

| Config | LinkedIn control | Mapping |
|---|---|---|
| `lookbackHours` | Date posted | ≤24 → `Past 24 hours`; ≤168 → `Past week`; ≤720 → `Past month`; larger → no date filter. Pick the closest bucket that **fully covers** the window, never a narrower one. |
| `employmentTypes` | Employment type | When it is a real subset, check exactly: `Full-time`, `Part-time`, `Contract`, `Temporary`, `Internship`, `Volunteer`. |
| `workModes` | Work mode / Remote | When it is a real subset of `Remote` / `Hybrid` / `On-site`, select the matching filter. |
| `seniority.include` | Experience level | Only when configured and the labels map unambiguously; otherwise skip the UI filter and judge on the page. |
| `countries`, `locations` | Location | Set the configured country; add cities only when `locations` is non-empty, and only if the location filter supports it. |

Do not add filters that are not in the config, such as salary, company, Easy Apply or applicant count. Use the visible controls; URL parameters like `f_TPR` and `f_JT` may be dropped by the AI search page, so do not rely on them.

If a filter cannot be applied, say so and read that field on each posting instead. Never assume the prompt filtered it.

## 3. Result extraction

- Job ID: the numeric ID in the card's link, e.g. `4487182341`.
- Canonical URL: `https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/<jobId>/`. Strip tracking parameters (`?trk=`, `?refId=`, `?trackingId=`, `?originalSubdomain=`).
- Company, title, location and posting age come from the card; the detail page wins on conflicts.
- Collect every card's canonical URL before opening details, then deduplicate.

## 4. Premium "You'd be a top applicant" prompt

Read this only when `linkedinPremium` is `true`. The account then shows a personal prompt on some jobs — **"You'd be a top applicant"**, **"You'd be a top applicant for this role"** or a **"Top applicant"** badge — on the result card and/or the detail page. Match it case-insensitively and accept both `'` and `’`; in a non-English UI, match its localized equivalent.

- Record it per vacancy for this run only (`topApplicant`, phrase verbatim, `card` / `detail`); do not persist it in the index. The detail page wins; a card-only prompt still counts.
- Never infer it from applicant counts, Easy Apply, search ranking or JD text. No visible prompt means no flag; `false` or absent skips this section without a limitation.
- It is ordering metadata, not a check. Classification is unchanged: a prompted job that fails any check (e.g. JD language) is excluded and stays out of the priority group.

## 5. Pagination

Advance with the results pagination control (or the next-page button). Stop when:

- the next page's postings are older than `lookbackHours`;
- LinkedIn reports no more results;
- the same postings repeat;
- a login wall, CAPTCHA or rate limit appears.

Record the displayed result count when the page shows one, plus the number of result pages actually opened and the stop reason.

## 6. Access boundaries

If LinkedIn requires login, shows a CAPTCHA, or blocks the run, stop this source and record it in `limitations`. Never ask for credentials, never bypass access controls, and never apply, message, save or follow anything.

## 7. Application-process fields

Record these while the job page is open. They are informational only and never affect match/review/excluded classification.

**Easy Apply:** `Yes` when the detail page shows an "Easy Apply" button that applies within LinkedIn; `No` when the apply button clearly redirects to the employer's site or an external application form; `Unknown` when neither is visible. Never infer it from applicant counts, Easy Apply badges on cards, or JD text.

**Cover letter:** `Yes` when the page or the Easy Apply flow explicitly states a cover letter is required; `No` when it explicitly states cover letter is optional or not needed; `Unknown` when neither is stated. Do not open the apply flow just to check — record only what is visible on the job page.

## 8. Known quirks

- The AI search page may reset filters after a new submission — re-apply and re-verify.
- The same role can appear under several job IDs, including multi-city and bilingual versions; that is handled by the soft-dedup rules in `job-index-and-audit.md`.
- `Easy Apply` is not a filter and must never be used as one.
